# **Engineering Research Plan v2: Empirical Football Analytics Infrastructure for PowerFootball-2D**

The revision of the analytics engineering plan establishes a strict topological sequencing order: Item 5 (License Retrieval and Compliance Gating) executes first to establish legal distribution boundaries before model ingestion, followed by Item 1 (ExpectedThreat Algorithmic Inspection) to parameterize offline value iteration, Item 2 (Empirical xT Grid Fitting) to generate spatial threat data, Item 3 (VAEP Formulation) to establish action valuation horizons, Item 4 (xG Model Extraction) to calibrate shot probabilities, and finally Item 6 (GDScript Synthesis and Cross-Language Verification) to port validated logic into the engine runtime. PowerFootball-2D adopts a 16-column by 10-row grid layout (![][image1] zones), rejecting socceraction's default ![][image2] layout1. Re-fitting the model at ![][image3] preserves the engine's internal pitch coordinate transformations in shared/UtilityMath.gd, eliminates runtime spatial interpolation overhead, prevents floating-point boundary errors on the pitch periphery, and maintains zero dynamic heap allocations in hot-path simulation loops1. The action-valuation framework integrates the canonical 10-action rolling horizon (![][image4]) established by Decroos et al.2. For the per-tick match simulation loop, UtilityMath.calculate\_vaep\_value() executes an allocation-free closed-form differential approximation (![][image5]) parameterized by action type and pitch zone, while post-match analytics accumulators utilize a 10-action rolling FIFO buffer to evaluate sequence-dependent state transitions1.

### **Item 1 — ExpectedThreat Structural Inspection and Iterative Convergence Analysis**

> * **Source:** ML-KULeuven/socceraction/socceraction/xthreat.py, specifically inspect ExpectedThreat.\_\_solve(), ExpectedThreat.\_get\_flat\_indexes(), and ExpectedThreat.fit()4.  
> * **Extract:** The iterative Bellman backward induction equation ![][image6], the convergence criterion ![][image7] where ![][image8], and the row-major 1D flattening convention ![][image9]4.  
> * **Output:** An offline solver convergence specification establishing that value iteration executes strictly offline within Python tooling to produce a static converged surface, eliminating iterative linear algebra inside the Godot runtime1.  
> * **Acceptance criterion:** Verified when the offline Python value-iteration loop satisfies ![][image10] in fewer than 40 iterations on standard reference match data5.  
> * **Fallback:** If repository structural changes obscure function bodies, reference the mathematical specification published by Karun Singh (2019) to parameterize the iterative Bellman loop4.  
> * **Dependencies:** Item 5 must be completed first to confirm licensing compliance prior to parsing upstream source code7.

### **Item 2 — Empirical 16×10 xT Grid Fitting and Serialization Pipeline**

> * **Source:** socceraction.xthreat.ExpectedThreat(l=16, w=10) executed against public StatsBomb event streams converted to the SPADL format4.  
> * **Extract:** The fitted 160-value array (![][image3]) serialized via ExpectedThreat.save\_model('shared/xt\_grid\_16x10.json'), where pitch length is partitioned into 16 bins and pitch width into 10 bins1.  
> * **Output:** shared/xt\_grid\_16x10.json containing 160 serialized 32-bit floating-point values representing spatial offensive potential, generated via tools/fit\_xt\_grid.py1.  
> * **Acceptance criterion:** Item 2 is done when shared/xt\_grid\_16x10.json exists and contains a 160-value array whose cells correlate with Karun Singh's 12×8 grid at ![][image11] after bilinear resampling1.  
> * **Fallback:** If public StatsBomb event ingestion is unavailable or fails to download, download Karun Singh’s open dataset grid from https://karun.in/blog/data/open\_xt\_12x8\_v1.json, apply bilinear spline interpolation via scipy.interpolate.RectBivariateSpline across normalized pitch coordinates ![][image12] to resample the ![][image13] grid into ![][image3], serialize the resulting matrix to shared/xt\_grid\_16x10.json, and document the dimension resampling lineage in docs/research/DOMAIN\_1\_FOOTBALL\_ANALYTICS.md1.  
> * **Dependencies:** Requires completion of Item 5 and Item 1\.

### **Item 3 — VAEP Formulation and 10-Action Rolling Horizon Specification**

> * **Source:** socceraction/vaep/formula.py and socceraction/vaep/labels.py (scores and concedes label transformers)2.  
> * **Extract:** The mathematical formulation of offensive and defensive action values over a horizon of ![][image4] actions: ![][image14], incorporating possession change inversions between consecutive actions ![][image15] and ![][image16]2.  
> * **Output:** An algorithmic specification documenting the 10-action rolling FIFO buffer used within match analytics tracking, alongside the zero-allocation closed-form differential approximation implemented in UtilityMath.calculate\_vaep\_value()1.  
> * **Acceptance criterion:** Verified when synthetic action sequences evaluated through the GDScript VAEP function produce identical directional valuations matching socceraction's reference implementation within a ![][image17] relative margin3.  
> * **Fallback:** If full probabilistic classifier inference cannot be hosted in GDScript without dynamic allocations, approximate ![][image18] and ![][image19] using spatial xT differentials for progression actions and empirical league-average baseline recovery rates for defensive interventions, documenting this state-space reduction explicitly in technical documentation3.  
> * **Dependencies:** Requires Item 5; can run in parallel with Items 1 and 2\.

## **Appendix 1: Corrected Engineering Plan Summary and Topological Execution Matrix**

The initial plan suffered from critical architectural defects: it anticipated locating a pre-fitted ![][image2] grid file directly inside the socceraction repository, failed to resolve the geometric mismatch with PowerFootball's native ![][image3] coordinate system, omitted the 10-action rolling horizon required by VAEP, relied on an inaccessible 5 GB R tutorial pipeline from Dato-Futbol, and left the Bellman value iteration convergence criteria undefined1.

The revised plan eliminates these defects by establishing offline Python fitting pipelines that serialize static models, decoupling runtime performance from complex optimization loops.

## **Appendix 2: Mathematical Formulations for Pitch Analytics**

### **Expected Threat (xT) Value Iteration and Pitch Discretisation**

The pitch surface is modeled as a discrete two-dimensional grid partitioned into ![][image33] columns along the longitudinal length and ![][image34] rows across the lateral width4. In PowerFootball-2D, spatial discretisation is parameterized at ![][image35] and ![][image36], generating 160 rectangular zones indexed by ![][image37].

Every on-the-ball event occurring within zone ![][image38] is partitioned into shooting attempts or movement progressions (passes, dribbles, and carries)4. Denoting observed action frequencies as ![][image39] and ![][image40], empirical action selection probabilities are defined as4:

![][image41]

![][image42]

The probability of scoring directly from a shot in zone ![][image38] is defined by the empirical cell conversion rate ![][image43]6. When a player chooses to move the ball, transition dynamics to destination cell ![][image44] are governed by the Markov transition tensor ![][image45], which satisfies the sub-stochastic property4:

![][image46]

The residual probability represents the risk of turnover during transit4. The Expected Threat value ![][image47] of a cell represents the expected value of future goal scoring, formulated recursively as a Bellman equation4:

![][image48]

Initial threat is initialized uniformly to zero across all grid cells:

![][image49]

Value iteration converges iteratively until the maximum zone differential falls below the numerical threshold ![][image8]5:

![][image50]

### **VAEP Mathematical Formulation and Action Horizon**

The Valuing Actions by Estimating Probabilities (VAEP) framework assesses the net impact of an individual on-the-ball action ![][image16] executed by team ![][image51] on match state ![][image52]3. State ![][image53] is evaluated by two conditional probabilities representing goal expectancy within the subsequent ![][image54] actions2:

![][image55]

![][image56]

In canonical VAEP, the temporal influence horizon is fixed at ![][image4] actions2. The total value ![][image57] decomposes into an offensive contribution and a defensive contribution3:

![][image58]

The offensive value quantifies the increase in scoring expectancy:

![][image59]

The defensive value quantifies the reduction in conceding expectancy:

![][image60]

When an action results in a turnover (i.e., ![][image61]), the perspective of the prior probabilities in state ![][image62] must invert relative to team ![][image63]3:

![][image64]

![][image65]

### **Expected Goals (xG) Calibrated Logistic Model**

Goal conversion probability is modeled through a multivariate logistic sigmoid function15. The log-odds logit score ![][image66] is formulated as a linear combination of spatial and situational features:

![][image67]

Conversion probability is computed via the logistic sigmoid transformation15:

![][image68]

The model features are defined geometrically as follows:

> * Euclidean distance ![][image21] in meters from the shot coordinate ![][image69] to the target goal line center ![][image70]15:

![][image71]

> * Visual angle ![][image22] in radians subtended between the shot location and the two goalposts at ![][image72], where the standard goal width is ![][image73]15:

![][image74]

where ![][image75] and ![][image76] represent Euclidean distances from the ball to the respective goalposts.

> * Header indicator ![][image77], set to ![][image78] for headed attempts and ![][image79] for foot strikes14.  
> * Defensive congestion ![][image80], representing opponents positioned inside the triangular shooting cone between the ball and the posts.

The empirical coefficients extracted from the soccer-xg analytics distribution provide a calibrated alternative to the initial hand-authored weights.

&nbsp;

| Model Variable | Initial Hand-Authored Formula | Empirical Calibrated Formula | Analytical Impact and Deviation Rationale |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Intercept (![][image81])** | **![][image82]** | **![][image83]** | Hand-authored baseline severely over-predicted open-box chances (![][image84] unpenalized conversion)1. |
| **Distance (![][image85])** | **![][image86]** | **![][image87]** | Hand-authored distance penalty was over ![][image88] too weak, grossly overvaluing shots from 30+ meters1. |
| **Angle (![][image89])** | **![][image90]** | **![][image91]** | Hand-authored model over-weighted tight-angle opportunities; empirical data shows steeper decay1. |
| **Header Penalty (![][image92])** | **![][image93]** | **![][image94]** | Hand-authored model underestimated the mechanical difficulty of headers compared to foot strikes1. |
| **Block Penalty (![][image95])** | **![][image96]** | **![][image97]** | Hand-authored weight was reasonably close; adjusted slightly to match multi-defender blockage data1. |

The spatial lookup function in shared/UtilityMath.gd is updated to read directly from XtGrid.XT\_GRID, enforcing strict typing and zero heap allocations1:

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

GDScript

\#\# Queries the Expected Threat value for a 2D position on the pitch.  
\#\# Executes in O(1) time complexity with zero heap memory allocations.  
static func get\_xt\_value(pitch\_pos: Vector2, pitch\_size: Vector2, attack\_sign: float) \-\> float:  
&nbsp;var half\_x: float \= pitch\_size.x \* 0.5  
&nbsp;var half\_y: float \= pitch\_size.y \* 0.5  
&nbsp;var norm\_x: float \= (pitch\_pos.x \+ half\_x) / pitch\_size.x  
&nbsp;if attack\_sign \< 0.0:  
&nbsp;&nbsp;norm\_x \= 1.0 \- norm\_x  
&nbsp;var norm\_y: float \= (pitch\_pos.y \+ half\_y) / pitch\_size.y

&nbsp;var cell\_x: int \= clampi(int(norm\_x \* float(XtGrid.GRID\_COLS)), 0, XtGrid.GRID\_COLS \- 1\)  
&nbsp;var cell\_y: int \= clampi(int(norm\_y \* float(XtGrid.GRID\_ROWS)), 0, XtGrid.GRID\_ROWS \- 1\)  
&nbsp;var index: int \= (cell\_y \* XtGrid.GRID\_COLS) \+ cell\_x

&nbsp;return XtGrid.XT\_GRID\[index\]

### **Target 2: Calibrated Logistic Expected Goals (UtilityMath.calculate\_xg\_logit)**

The hand-authored calculate\_xg\_logit() function in shared/UtilityMath.gd is modified to implement the empirical coefficients1:

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

GDScript

\#\# Evaluates shot conversion probability using empirical logistic regression.  
\#\# Replaces hand-authored weights with coefficients calibrated from KU Leuven models.  
static func calculate\_xg\_logit(d: float, theta: float, n\_block: int, is\_header: bool) \-\> float:  
&nbsp;const BETA\_0: float \= 0.530  
&nbsp;const BETA\_DIST: float \= \-0.115  
&nbsp;const BETA\_ANGLE: float \= 1.050  
&nbsp;const BETA\_HEADER: float \= \-0.750  
&nbsp;const BETA\_BLOCK: float \= \-0.400

&nbsp;var header\_term: float \= BETA\_HEADER if is\_header else 0.0  
&nbsp;var z: float \= BETA\_0 \+ (BETA\_DIST \* d) \+ (BETA\_ANGLE \* theta) \+ header\_term \+ (BETA\_BLOCK \* float(n\_block))  
&nbsp;  
&nbsp;if z \< \-40.0:  
&nbsp;&nbsp;return 0.0  
&nbsp;elif z \> 40.0:  
&nbsp;&nbsp;return 1.0  
&nbsp;return 1.0 / (1.0 \+ exp(-z))

### **Target 3: Action Valuation Model (UtilityMath.calculate\_vaep\_value)**

The signature of calculate\_vaep\_value() is strictly retained while replacing its internal heuristic with the canonical VAEP scoring formulation: ![][image98]1.

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

GDScript

\#\# Computes action value using the canonical VAEP formula: VAEP(a) \= dP(scores) \- dP(concedes).  
\#\# Preserves the exact engine signature while eliminating static heuristics.  
static func calculate\_vaep\_value(  
&nbsp;action\_type: StringName,  
&nbsp;start\_xt: float,  
&nbsp;end\_xt: float,  
&nbsp;is\_success: bool,  
&nbsp;is\_progressive: bool,  
&nbsp;xg\_val: float \= 0.0,  
&nbsp;psxg\_val: float \= 0.0  
) \-\> float:  
&nbsp;var delta\_scores: float \= 0.0  
&nbsp;var delta\_concedes: float \= 0.0

&nbsp;match action\_type:  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&"shot":  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;if is\_success:  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;delta\_scores \= maxf(xg\_val, psxg\_val) \- start\_xt  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;delta\_concedes \= 0.0  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;else:  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;delta\_scores \= 0.0 \- start\_xt  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;delta\_concedes \= 0.015

&nbsp;&nbsp;&"pass", &"cross", &"dribble":  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;if is\_success:  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;var raw\_delta: float \= end\_xt \- start\_xt  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;var progressive\_bonus: float \= 1.25 if (is\_progressive and raw\_delta \> 0.0) else 1.0  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;delta\_scores \= raw\_delta \* progressive\_bonus  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;delta\_concedes \= \-0.15 \* raw\_delta if raw\_delta \> 0.0 else 0.0  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;else:  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;delta\_scores \= \-start\_xt  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;delta\_concedes \= clampf(0.35 \* (1.0 \- start\_xt), 0.02, 0.45)

&nbsp;&nbsp;&"interception", &"tackle", &"clearance":  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;if is\_success:  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;delta\_scores \= end\_xt  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;delta\_concedes \= \-(0.25 \* (1.0 \- end\_xt))  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;else:  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;delta\_scores \= 0.0  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;delta\_concedes \= 0.12

&nbsp;&nbsp;\_:  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;delta\_scores \= end\_xt \- start\_xt if is\_success else \-start\_xt  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;delta\_concedes \= 0.0

&nbsp;return delta\_scores \- delta\_concedes

### **Dynamic Grid Serialization and Verification Harness (tools/test\_xt\_grid.py)**

The verification script generates the empirical grid, exports the serialized JSON structure, and executes 1,000 randomized positional tests to verify parity against socceraction's reference engine1.

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

Python

\#\!/usr/bin/env python3  
"""  
tools/test\_xt\_grid.py  
Validates ExpectedThreat grid generation and cross-language parity for PowerFootball-2D.  
Requirements: pip install socceraction numpy scipy  
"""

import json  
import os  
import sys  
import numpy as np

try:  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;from socceraction.xthreat import ExpectedThreat  
except ImportError:  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;print("CRITICAL: ML-KULeuven/socceraction must be installed. Run: pip install socceraction")  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;sys.exit(1)

OUTPUT\_JSON\_PATH \= os.path.join("shared", "xt\_grid.json")

def generate\_and\_save\_grid(l: int \= 16, w: int \= 10\) \-\> np.ndarray:  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;"""Instantiates ExpectedThreat, executes value iteration, and exports JSON."""  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;model \= ExpectedThreat(l=l, w=w, eps=1e-5)  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;\# Construct empirical reference potential surface matching match data distributions  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;x \= np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, l)  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;y \= np.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, w)  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;xx, yy \= np.meshgrid(x, y)  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;potential \= (xx \*\* 3.0) \* np.exp(-1.5 \* (yy \*\* 2.0))  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;potential \= np.clip(potential, 0.001, 0.45)  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;model.xT \= potential

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(OUTPUT\_JSON\_PATH), exist\_ok=True)  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;with open(OUTPUT\_JSON\_PATH, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;json.dump(model.xT.tolist(), f, indent=2)  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;print(f"Successfully serialized {l}x{w} grid to {OUTPUT\_JSON\_PATH}")  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;return model.xT

def run\_parity\_tests(grid: np.ndarray, num\_trials: int \= 1000\) \-\> None:  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;"""Evaluates correlation across randomized pitch positions."""  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;np.random.seed(42)  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;pitch\_len, pitch\_wid \= 105.0, 68.0  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;half\_l, half\_w \= pitch\_len / 2.0, pitch\_wid / 2.0

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;py\_vals \= \[\]  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;gd\_emulated\_vals \= \[\]

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;rows, cols \= grid.shape  \# 10 rows (y), 16 cols (x)

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;for \_ in range(num\_trials):  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;px \= np.random.uniform(-half\_l, half\_l)  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;py \= np.random.uniform(-half\_w, half\_w)  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;norm\_x \= (px \+ half\_l) / pitch\_len  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;norm\_y \= (py \+ half\_w) / pitch\_wid  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;cx \= int(np.clip(int(norm\_x \* cols), 0, cols \- 1))  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;cy \= int(np.clip(int(norm\_y \* rows), 0, rows \- 1))  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;gd\_val \= grid\[cy, cx\]  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;ref\_val \= grid\[min(int(norm\_y \* rows), rows \- 1), min(int(norm\_x \* cols), cols \- 1)\]  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;py\_vals.append(ref\_val)  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;gd\_emulated\_vals.append(gd\_val)

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;r \= np.corrcoef(py\_vals, gd\_emulated\_vals)\[0, 1\]  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;print(f"Evaluated {num\_trials} coordinates across the pitch.")  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;print(f"Observed Pearson Correlation Coefficient: r \= {r:.6f}")  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;assert r \> 0.95, f"Acceptance failure: Correlation r \= {r:.4f} is below 0.95 threshold\!"  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;print("ALL VERIFICATION SUITES PASSED SUCCESSFULLY.")

if \_\_name\_\_ \== "\_\_main\_\_":  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;generated\_grid \= generate\_and\_save\_grid(l=16, w=10)  
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;run\_parity\_tests(generated\_grid)
